label: /speckit:save's mandated continuity writer is the compiled runtime/cli/dist/continuity/generate-context.js, which is gitignored by the blanket dist/ rule (.gitignore:60) and has zero tracked files (git ls-files | wc -l = 0). Nothing provisions it on clone: the root runtime build (package.json:17) runs tsc --build against a tsconfig that excludes cli/** (tsconfig.json:47), and neither manifest carries prepare/postinstall/prepack. The CLI's own build (cli/package.json:13) is reachable only from inside runtime/cli and auto-triggers only via pretest (cli/package.json:18); CI builds the root package only (changed-packet-validation.yml:53, spec-kit-check.yml:123). Fresh clone: /speckit:save fails with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND. Working checkout: save runs unattested local bytes, so the writer version behind a packet's _memory.continuity is unrecoverable from the repository.

check-source-dist-alignment.ts detects orphans only: it maps each dist *.js to a source .ts and fails when none exists (success line at :380 scopes the claim to 'every scanned dist *.js file maps to a source .ts file'), performing no fs.stat, mtime or content comparison. A dist file that exists but predates its source passes cleanly, and the file's own comment at :256 concedes 'stale bytes too ... they drift the moment the source changes'. The second question - is that dist current? - is exactly what F1's failure mode depends on.

The source/dist alignment eval is wired into the CLI package's check aggregate (cli/package.json:24) but is referenced by no CI workflow: a grep of .github/workflows/*.yml for check-source-dist-alignment matches nothing, and the workflows touch the runtime only to npm run build and to call validate.sh. The one gate that would notice a dist file whose source was deleted is voluntary.

Supersedes iteration 16's V6. runtime/dist/core/config.js not exporting resolveProjectRoot is a path collision, not drift: the source runtime/cli/core/config.ts:131 compiles to runtime/cli/dist/core/config.js, which does export it at :70 and carries the source's own loader banner at :7. runtime/dist/core/config.js is an unrelated module of server path and rate-limit constants (SERVER_DIR, NODE_MODULES, INDEX_SCAN_COOLDOWN, MAX_QUERY_LENGTH at :9). No caller throws. The residual worth keeping is that core/config resolves to two unrelated modules depending on compilation root.

A HARD-block comment rule carries a standing documented exemption. ALLOWLIST_EXCEPTIONS in the alignment eval embeds ephemeral finding ids and a packet number in three reason strings (F-020-D5-02, F-020-D5-03, 'deleted in packet 007' at :76 and :82), while the repository ships .github/workflows/comment-hygiene.yml for exactly this. A prior remediation packet recorded this file's allowlist reasons as an explicit out-of-scope exemption, so the rule is HARD-block in canon and exempted in practice at this site. The durable WHY ('orphan from a source move, pending removal in a dist-cleanup follow-on') survives deletion of every identifier.

A missing dist is deliberately invisible to the freshness guard. The CLI tree is a registered package with a rebuild command (dist-freshness.cjs:46,:53), but an absent or unbuildable checkout is classified unprovisioned with stale:false (:201), justified at :178 as 'a provisioning gap, not source drift'. The reasoning is sound for a bare worktree the guard cannot fix, yet at the operator's moment of need it says 'not stale' about a checkout where /speckit:save is about to fail outright. save.md and memory-system.md should name the bootstrap (cd runtime/cli && npm run build) as a precondition.

direction: Export-count divergence between TypeScript source and compiled .d.ts in the sampled cli/core and lib modules
reason: All five mechanical mismatches (find-predecessor-memory 3v4, thin-continuity-record 24v25, entity-extractor 7v8, access-telemetry 6v7, orchestrator 11v12) are exactly the .d.ts trailer 'export {};' plus a sourceMappingURL comment, which has no source analogue. Each module's dist is export-complete. The counting method was wrong, not the artifacts.

direction: .opencode/skills and .pi/skills hold duplicated copies of the system-spec-kit skill tree
